topicTitle: 14.2 General Methods of Preparations of Alkanes
stem: How can alkanes be prepared by hydrogenation of alkynes and alkyl halides? Give a balanced equation for each.
modelAnswer: Hydrogenation of an alkyne: $\mathrm{CH}_{3}-\mathrm{C}\equiv\mathrm{CH}+2\mathrm{H}_{2}\rightarrow\mathrm{CH}_{3}-\mathrm{CH}_{2}-\mathrm{CH}_{3}$, using Ni and heat. Reduction of an alkyl halide: $\mathrm{CH}_{3}\mathrm{CH}_{2}\mathrm{CH}_{2}\mathrm{Cl}+2[\mathrm{H}]\rightarrow\mathrm{CH}_{3}\mathrm{CH}_{2}\mathrm{CH}_{3}+\mathrm{HCl}$, using Zn in aqueous acid.

topicTitle: 14.2 General Methods of Preparations of Alkanes
stem: Explain preparation of alkanes by hydrogenation of alkenes and cracking of larger hydrocarbons.
modelAnswer: Alkane preparation by hydrogenation: an alkene reacts with H2 over finely divided Ni at 200-300°C to form the corresponding alkane. By cracking: a larger hydrocarbon is heated at 450-750°C and high pressure to form smaller alkanes and alkenes.

stem: Explain how alkanes can be prepared from CH3–C≡CH, CH3–C≡C–CH3 and CH3CH2CH2Cl, mentioning the reaction type in each case.
modelAnswer: $\mathrm{CH}_{3}-\mathrm{C}\equiv\mathrm{CH}+2\mathrm{H}_{2}\rightarrow\mathrm{CH}_{3}\mathrm{CH}_{2}\mathrm{CH}_{3}$ by hydrogenation; $\mathrm{CH}_{3}-\mathrm{C}\equiv\mathrm{C}-\mathrm{CH}_{3}+2\mathrm{H}_{2}\rightarrow\mathrm{CH}_{3}\mathrm{CH}_{2}\mathrm{CH}_{2}\mathrm{CH}_{3}$ by hydrogenation; $\mathrm{CH}_{3}\mathrm{CH}_{2}\mathrm{CH}_{2}\mathrm{Cl}+2[\mathrm{H}]\rightarrow\mathrm{CH}_{3}\mathrm{CH}_{2}\mathrm{CH}_{3}+\mathrm{HCl}$ by reduction with Zn in aqueous acid. The reaction types are hydrogenation, hydrogenation and reduction, respectively.

topicTitle: 14.3 Properties of Alkanes
stem: Give chemical reactions of alkanes for complete combustion and incomplete combustion.
modelAnswer: Complete combustion: CH4 + 2O2 -> CO2 + 2H2O + heat. Incomplete combustion with limited oxygen can be represented as 2CH4 + 3O2 -> 2CO + 4H2O + heat.

topicTitle: 14.3 Properties of Alkanes
stem: Write the reactions of CH4 with Cl2 in diffused sunlight/UV light and in direct sunlight.
modelAnswer: In diffused sunlight: $\mathrm{CH}_{4}+\mathrm{Cl}_{2}\rightarrow\mathrm{CH}_{3}\mathrm{Cl}+\mathrm{HCl}$. In direct sunlight: $\mathrm{CH}_{4}+2\mathrm{Cl}_{2}\rightarrow\mathrm{C}+4\mathrm{HCl}$. The first is mono-substitution; the direct-sunlight reaction is explosive.

topicTitle: 14.3 Properties of Alkanes
stem: Sunlight in methane/chlorine substitution reaction.
modelAnswer: In diffused sunlight, methane and chlorine undergo substitution: CH4 + Cl2 -> CH3Cl + HCl. In direct sunlight, the reaction is explosive and forms carbon and HCl: CH4 + 2Cl2 -> C + 4HCl.

topicTitle: 14.3 Properties of Alkanes
stem: How can sunlight be important in substitution reaction of methane with chlorine? Explain with reactions.
modelAnswer: Sunlight initiates substitution of methane with chlorine. In diffused sunlight: $\mathrm{CH}_{4}+\mathrm{Cl}_{2}\rightarrow\mathrm{CH}_{3}\mathrm{Cl}+\mathrm{HCl}$; in direct sunlight: $\mathrm{CH}_{4}+2\mathrm{Cl}_{2}\rightarrow\mathrm{C}+4\mathrm{HCl}$.
